description: Deep Contextual Video Compression (DCVC) family architecture decomposed. DCVC replaces the conventional codec's transform + entropy coding stages with learned neural networks. The key architectural insight: instead of computing 'predictor + residual', DCVC computes a 'contextualised feature' from the past frame, then conditionally compresses the current frame's features given that context. The successor versions (DCVC-DC, DCVC-FM, DCVC-RT) each refine the architecture for compression efficiency, speed, or both.

sub_mechanisms.name: feature_encoder_network
sub_mechanisms.definition: A CNN that maps the input frame x_t to a latent feature representation z_t. Typically 4-5 conv layers with strides downsampling spatial resolution by 2x each.
sub_mechanisms.why: The encoder learns a transform optimised for the data distribution. Unlike DCT (fixed basis), the learned features can capture textures, edges, and motion-like patterns directly relevant to compression. The CNN backbone determines the achievable compression ceiling.

sub_mechanisms.name: context_encoder
sub_mechanisms.definition: Network that processes the previously-decoded frame and motion vectors to produce a context feature c_t. Used as conditioning for the current frame's entropy model.
sub_mechanisms.why: Captures everything the decoder already knows. The current frame's entropy is reduced by knowing what's predictable from context. This replaces conventional 'predictor' + 'residual' decomposition with a more general 'features conditioned on context'.

sub_mechanisms.name: motion_estimation_network
sub_mechanisms.definition: A separate CNN that estimates optical flow between current frame and reference. Outputs a per-sample motion vector field (dense rather than block-based).
sub_mechanisms.why: Dense motion captures non-rigid motion (foliage, water, deformation) that block-based motion can't. The network can learn motion patterns specific to natural video, beating hand-designed optical-flow algorithms on compression-relevant metrics.

sub_mechanisms.name: motion_compensation_warp
sub_mechanisms.definition: Differentiable warping operator that applies the motion field to the reference feature map, producing a warped context feature.
sub_mechanisms.why: Differentiable warping lets the motion estimation be trained end-to-end via gradients flowing back from the entropy/reconstruction losses. Hand-designed (non-differentiable) warping would break the training pipeline.

sub_mechanisms.name: hyperprior_network
sub_mechanisms.definition: Auxiliary network that estimates per-sample parameters (mean and scale) of a Gaussian distribution for each latent feature. Encoded as a small 'hyperprior' bitstream sent alongside the latent.
sub_mechanisms.why: Closes the loop between encoder and decoder: the decoder knows the per-sample probability distribution to decode the latent. The hyperprior is small (~1% of total bits) but enables accurate entropy estimation, which is the compression gain.

sub_mechanisms.name: conditional_entropy_model
sub_mechanisms.definition: Entropy model that conditions the current frame's latent z_t on the context c_t. Computes P(z_t | c_t) and uses it to compress z_t via arithmetic coding.
sub_mechanisms.why: Conditional entropy H(Z|C) is lower than marginal H(Z) when context is predictive. This is the core compression mechanism in DCVC — the better the context model, the lower the bitcost.

sub_mechanisms.name: feature_decoder_network
sub_mechanisms.definition: A CNN that maps the decoded latent z_t back to the reconstructed frame x_t_hat. Mirror of the encoder, with transposed convolutions or upsampling.
sub_mechanisms.why: Inverts the encoder transform. Trained jointly with the encoder so that reconstruction quality is maximised under the bit budget.

sub_mechanisms.name: end_to_end_training
sub_mechanisms.definition: Loss function: L = lambda * R + D, where R is the estimated bitrate (from the entropy model) and D is the reconstruction distortion (MSE or MS-SSIM). All networks trained jointly via backprop.
sub_mechanisms.why: End-to-end optimisation of the rate-distortion trade-off. The encoder learns to produce latents that are compressible AND reconstructible. Each component informs the others' training. Conventional codecs train each stage independently, leaving compression efficiency on the table.

sub_mechanisms.name: DCVC_DC_feature_modulation
sub_mechanisms.definition: DCVC-DC's innovation: feature modulation layers that scale the encoder's intermediate features based on context. Different parts of the feature map get different processing.
sub_mechanisms.why: Context isn't equally relevant everywhere — a moving region needs different treatment than a static one. Feature modulation lets the encoder adapt its processing per region without explicit region segmentation. Enables ~30% bitrate saving over DCVC.

sub_mechanisms.name: DCVC_FM_diverse_contexts
sub_mechanisms.definition: DCVC-FM adds multiple parallel context streams (long-term, short-term, motion) merged at the entropy model.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different content benefits from different context types. Foreground objects need short-term reference; backgrounds benefit from longer-term temporal aggregation. Multiple contexts give the entropy model more information at minimal extra compute.

sub_mechanisms.name: DCVC_RT_efficient_backbone
sub_mechanisms.definition: DCVC-RT's contribution: a smaller, faster network backbone (mobile architectures like MobileNetV3 building blocks) that runs at 100+ FPS for 1080p.
sub_mechanisms.why: Deployment requires speed. The DCVC-DC compression ceiling is held while throughput jumps 10-30x. Trade-offs: some compression efficiency lost, but the efficiency loss is small and the throughput gain enables real-time use.

sub_mechanisms.name: single_model_rate_control
sub_mechanisms.definition: DCVC-FM and DCVC-RT use a single trained model that supports a wide range of rate-distortion points (via a scalar 'lambda' input).
sub_mechanisms.why: Conventional learned codecs needed one model per quality level (one for 1 Mbps, another for 5 Mbps, etc.). Single-model rate control trains one universal model. Lower memory footprint + simpler deployment.

derivation_rules.name: learned_transform_beats_dct_for_specific_data_distribution
if: a transform is trained on the data distribution it will encode
then: it captures content-specific structure DCT cannot
derivation_rules.why: DCT is optimal for AR(1) signals but real video isn't perfectly AR(1). Learned transforms specialise to the actual distribution. The gain is bounded by the gap between AR(1) and real-video statistics — typically 10-20% at high quality, larger at low quality.

derivation_rules.name: conditional_entropy_drops_below_marginal_when_context_helps
if: the context is predictive of the current frame's latent
then: the conditional entropy H(z_t | c_t) is below the marginal H(z_t)
derivation_rules.why: Information theory. The amount of conditional-entropy reduction is exactly the mutual information between context and latent. DCVC's architectural choices (context encoder + entropy model) maximise this mutual information.

derivation_rules.name: end_to_end_training_extracts_more_than_per_stage
derivation_rules.why: Joint optimisation finds the global trade-off, not local. Conventional codecs leave gains on the table because their transform / quantisation / entropy stages are designed independently. End-to-end learning captures the inter-stage interactions.

derivation_rules.name: dense_motion_beats_block_motion_for_nonrigid
derivation_rules.why: Block motion forces all samples in a block to share a motion vector. Non-rigid motion violates this. Dense per-sample motion captures it, at the cost of more bits to encode the motion itself. The per-sample motion is itself compressible via the learned motion network.

derivation_rules.name: throughput_pareto_dominates_at_real_time
then: it becomes a candidate for production deployment
derivation_rules.why: Production codecs need to run at content rate (24-60 fps). DCVC-RT was the first learned codec at this throughput. Below real-time, learned codecs were academic curiosities; at real-time, they become deployable.
